quests.title: half six at Austinmer
quests.blurb: Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. I start at half six and for a month the Austinmer back lane has had somebody in it who is not waiting for bread. It started small, the way these things do. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

steps.label: the lane, from the door, no flash
I am not calling anyone until I am sure

quests.title: The Lane Light, Austinmer
quests.blurb: I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. A light on that lane costs Austinmer $105 and the landlord has said no twice, so we are doing it ourselves. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. I would rather know than wonder.

steps.label: $105 and I will fit it myself
do not tell him where it came from

quests.title: Flour Run, Austinmer
quests.blurb: You will think I am making this up. The flour for Austinmer comes off a truck at half six and last a public holiday nobody remembered the truck came and the flour did not. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. That's the whole job. No catch.

steps.label: ride out to Thirroul where the load is made up
the pallet with our name on it, if it exists

quests.title: The Loading Zone, Austinmer
quests.blurb: There is no clever way to say this. The Austinmer loading zone has had a car in it at half six every morning this week and the driver waits in it, which makes it worse. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.

steps.label: the one who says he is only a minute
and the ticket I got, off him

quests.title: The Sourdough Sign, Austinmer
quests.blurb: You look like you have twenty minutes. Somebody two doors down from Austinmer put up a sign on a public holiday nobody remembered that says the same six words as ours, in the same order. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. Take your time. Do not take a week.

steps.label: walk down and read it properly
both signs if you can get them in one frame
tell me I am not imagining it

quests.title: The Old Site, Austinmer
quests.blurb: Keep it between us for now. This business was at Thirroul before it was at Austinmer, and there is a woman there who still has the original book. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Come and find me after, either way.

steps.label: she is usually about in the afternoon
bring back whatever she is willing to say

quests.title: The Strathfield Pool
quests.blurb: Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. Council has been saying the Strathfield pool is at end of life since grand final week and the crack they keep pointing at is not in the shell. It started small, the way these things do. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

steps.label: the crack, close, with something for scale
an engineer can read that. A councillor cannot.

quests.title: The Petition Stall, Strathfield
quests.blurb: I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. We are running a stall for Strathfield on grand final week and a stall needs $129 of gear that nobody has volunteered to pay for. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. I would rather know than wonder.

steps.label: $129 and a table, if you see one
I will be there from eight either way

quests.title: Squad, Strathfield
quests.blurb: You will think I am making this up. I coach 38 kids at Strathfield at first light and three of them have stopped coming without anybody ringing me. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. That's the whole job. No catch.

steps.label: the flats where two of them live
take something with you, it is a long walk up
I do not need them back. I need to know.

quests.title: The Deep End, Strathfield
quests.blurb: There is no clever way to say this. A group has been coming over the Strathfield fence after close and swimming in the dark, which is how Strathfield loses its pool. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.

steps.label: the ones who go over the fence
the spot in the fence they use

quests.title: The Kiosk Freezer, Strathfield
quests.blurb: You look like you have twenty minutes. The kiosk at Strathfield has a bucket of odd keys in it and a freezer that has been running warm since grand final week. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. Take your time. Do not take a week.

steps.label: get two, we are going to be here
the plant room behind the kiosk
tell me whether it is the freezer or the power

quests.title: The Aquatic Centre, Strathfield
quests.blurb: Keep it between us for now. They want everyone from Strathfield to drive to the new centre at Homebush, so somebody should go and see whether it is any good. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Come and find me after, either way.

steps.label: have a proper look, not a quick one
be honest with me, even if it is nice

quests.title: The Wentworthville Rank
quests.blurb: Honestly, I am past caring how it looks. The rank outside Wentworthville used to hold nine cars and since the first of the month it holds four, and nobody will say who moved the line. It started small, the way these things do. Whatever it costs you, tell me and I will cover it.

steps.label: the painted line and the old one under it
the old paint is still there, that is the whole argument

quests.title: Lost Fares, Wentworthville
quests.blurb: I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. Since the rank at Wentworthville shrank I am $120 a week down, and the association wants that number from somebody who can prove it. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. I would rather know than wonder.

steps.label: $120 in a week, to show it can be done
that is the submission, right there

quests.title: Queue Jumpers, Wentworthville
quests.blurb: You will think I am making this up. Cars that have never sat in the Wentworthville queue turn up at knock-off and take the front of it, and the drivers who waited say nothing. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. That's the whole job. No catch.

steps.label: the ones who take the front
$43, which is about one airport run

quests.title: The Late Train, Wentworthville
quests.blurb: There is no clever way to say this. When the last train into Wentworthville is late, 43 people come out at once and I have to have cars there before they do. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.

steps.label: come in on the last one from Westmead and see it
the rank at the moment the doors open

quests.title: The Door, Wentworthville
quests.blurb: You look like you have twenty minutes. I have stood on this door near Wentworthville for 43 years and since the first of the month somebody has been sending my guests to a different rank. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. Take your time. Do not take a week.

steps.label: follow one of them and see where they end up
you will be standing about, get something

quests.title: The Depot, Wentworthville
quests.blurb: Keep it between us for now. The plates working the Wentworthville rank are dispatched from a depot at Westmead, and the man who runs it has never met a driver he liked. The paperwork says one thing and my eyes say another. Come and find me after, either way.

steps.label: go and be pleasant at him anyway
tell me whether he is the problem or the symptom
